2608.14014.title: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In?
2608.14014.paper_summary: Two old market sayings hold that news is already priced in by the time it is published, and that the rumor is bought while the news is sold. Both place the price move associated with a piece of news before and at publication rather than after it. Whether the claims hold, for which kinds of news, and by how much are basic questions about how fast markets absorb public information. We test them on 4.57 million financial news articles covering roughly 3,000 US stocks (2023-2026). A large language model teacher, distilled into a compact classifier through active learning, assigns each article one of 17 event tags and five attributes; articles are clustered into stories to separate first reports from follow-up coverage; and beta-adjusted abnormal returns are measured around the resulting 1.68 million stock-day events, with 364,405 neutral-sentiment events as a placebo group. Three results follow. First, the price move associated with news concentrates before and at publication: pooled across all signed events, the cumulative move in the news direction by the close of publication day is 2.8 times its value 20 days later, and for rumor-flagged events the rumor day captures the entire move while the subsequent confirmation contributes nothing. Second, measured against the placebo of comparable stocks, markets underreact to numbers and overreact to stories: quantified fundamental news (earnings, dividends, guidance, analyst actions) keeps drifting in the direction of the news for weeks, while soft story-driven news (launches, macro commentary, leadership) gives back its move. Third, news carries width as well as direction: publicity raises volatility before the publication day, and volatility declines once the news is out, because publication resolves uncertainty. The study also produces a table of measured drift for each event tag, usable as a prior in news-conditioned forecasting models.
2608.14014.paper_summary_zh: 兩句古老的市場格言認為，新聞在發佈時已經被定價，並且謠言在新聞被出售時被購買。這兩者都將與新聞相關的價格變動置於發佈之前及發佈時，而非之後。這些主張是否成立、適用於哪些類型的新聞以及程度如何，都是關於市場吸收公共信息速度的基本問題。我們對涵蓋大約 3,000 支美國股票的 4.57 百萬篇金融新聞文章進行了測試（2023-2026）。一個大型語言模型教師，通過主動學習濃縮成一個緊湊的分類器，為每篇文章分配 17 種事件標籤和五個屬性；文章被聚類成故事，以區分首次報導和後續報導；並且在結果中 1.68 百萬的股票日事件周圍測量經過 beta 調整的異常回報，364,405 個中性情緒事件作為安慰劑組。隨之而來有三個結果。首先，與新聞相關的價格變動集中在發佈之前和發佈時：在所有簽名事件中，發佈日收盤時的累計變動是 20 天後的 2.8 倍，而對於標記為謠言的事件，謠言日捕捉了整個變動，而隨後的確認則沒有貢獻。其次，與可比股票的安慰劑相比，市場對數字反應不足，對故事反應過度：量化的基本新聞（收益、股息、指導、分析師行動）在數週內持續向新聞方向漂移，而以故事驅動的軟新聞（發布、宏觀評論、領導）則回吐其變動。第三，新聞同時帶有寬度和方向：在發佈日前，宣傳提高了波動性，而一旦新聞發布，波動性便下降，因為發佈解決了不確定性。該研究還生成了一個每個事件標籤的測量漂移表，可用作新聞條件預測模型中的先驗。
